rationale: Collection member S9.664, Neuroprotective potential of intracellular acidification in a toxic model of Parkinson disease: rotenone was delivered in olive oil vehicle to 12-month CD-1 mice; treatment was exercise/CO2 and outcomes were locomotion/coordination. Oil is a vehicle, not the treatment; no apathy or refining details.
Collection member P-02.1-03, extra-virgin olive-oil phenolics oleacein/oleocanthal and tumor-cell autophagy. This is a different preparation, cancer-cell endpoint, and no Parkinson/apathy population.

BNA 2017 abstract book body: olive oil appears as vehicle/control in a mouse liver-fibrosis experiment; apathy appears in separate Parkinson reward/decision-making abstracts. They are different members and do not link olive oil to apathy.

Independent direct refined-oil exposure (NCT03824197; AU-ROOAD): 30 mL/day raw Bertolli Extra Light refined olive oil with null phenolics for 6 months, ROO n=12 vs EVOO n=13, in MCI (25 completed). CDR/behavioral and imaging outcomes; apathy not measured and population is not PD. ROO CDR changed within-arm, but between-oil differences were not significant.

PD cross-sectional study measured apathy among nonmotor outcomes, but exposure was dietary-pattern scores (MIND/DII/HDI), not isolated or refined olive oil. Publisher text says apathy was rated by UPDRS items; no olive-oil-specific effect can be assigned.

PD case-control study used food-frequency questionnaire for olive oil and other cooking oils and related consumption to PD odds/UPDRS; olive-oil type/refinement was not specified and apathy was not a separately reported outcome. Actual intake route, not exact refined-oil/apathy evidence.
